title: Overlapping wildcard hosts across VirtualServices now resolve to the most specific match, not the oldest VirtualService

detection.reason: whether two VirtualServices' hosts overlap is a cross-object comparison the evaluator does not make; the projection carries each VirtualService's hosts

quote: Previously, the oldest VirtualService would take precedence regardless of whether or not it was the most specific host match. Now, the most specific host match will take precedence.
remediation: Where two VirtualServices claim overlapping wildcard hosts (`*.example.com` and `api.example.com`), traffic that used to follow the older VirtualService now follows the more specific host. Check the listed wildcard-host VirtualServices for overlaps; to keep the old order set `PERSIST_OLDEST_FIRST_HEURISTIC_FOR_VIRTUAL_SERVICE_HOST_MATCHING=true` on istiod (removed again in 1.24).
verifyCommand: kubectl get virtualservices.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.hosts[]? | startswith("*")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + (.spec.hosts | join(","))'  # printed VirtualServices carry wildcard hosts; any host they overlap with now wins by specificity

title: SNI is now set automatically from the HTTP host header when a DestinationRule does not set it

detection.reason: the projection carries a DestinationRule's TLS mode and which TLS keys it sets, but the SNI a proxy will send is computed per request

quote: auto_sni is enabled by default. This means SNI will be set automatically based on the downstream HTTP host/authority header if `DestinationRule` does not explicitly set the same.
remediation: TLS-originating DestinationRules (`tls.mode: SIMPLE` or `MUTUAL`) without an explicit `sni` now send the request's host header as SNI. Upstreams that reject unexpected SNI need an explicit `tls.sni`; otherwise no action. To keep the old behaviour use `compatibilityVersion: 1.20` (that profile is removed at 1.24; the flag itself at 1.26).
verifyCommand: kubectl get destinationrules.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.trafficPolicy.tls.mode // "") | test("^(SIMPLE|MUTUAL)$")) | select(.spec.trafficPolicy.tls.sni == null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " host=" + .spec.host'  # a printed DestinationRule originates TLS without an explicit sni and now sends the host header as SNI

title: Sidecars now verify upstream TLS certificates against the OS CA bundle when a DestinationRule sets no caCertificates

detection.reason: the projection carries a DestinationRule's TLS mode and which TLS keys it sets; whether the upstream's certificate chains to the OS bundle is not on the cluster

quote: This means server certificates will be automatically verified using the OS CA certificates when not using a DestinationRule caCertificates field.
remediation: Every TLS-originating DestinationRule (`tls.mode: SIMPLE`/`MUTUAL`) that sets neither `caCertificates` nor `insecureSkipVerify` now fails the handshake against a self-signed or private-CA upstream. Add `caCertificates` (or `credentialName` with a CA), set `insecureSkipVerify: true` where verification is not wanted, or install with `compatibilityVersion: 1.20` — a stopgap: 1.24 removes that profile and the flag.
verifyCommand: kubectl get destinationrules.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.trafficPolicy.tls.mode // "") | test("^(SIMPLE|MUTUAL)$")) | select(.spec.trafficPolicy.tls.caCertificates == null and .spec.trafficPolicy.tls.credentialName == null and .spec.trafficPolicy.tls.insecureSkipVerify != true) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " host=" + .spec.host'  # a printed DestinationRule originates TLS with no CA and no insecureSkipVerify — its upstream certificate is now verified against the OS bundle

title: ExternalName Services are now aliases — VirtualServices routing to them and DestinationRules on them stop applying

detection.reason: names every ExternalName Service; whether a VirtualService or DestinationRule references it is stated in the remediation, not tested here

quote: `VirtualServices` that route to an `ExternalName` service will no longer work unless the referenced service exists (as a Service or ServiceEntry). * `DestinationRule` can no longer apply to `ExternalName` services. Instead, create rules where the `host` references service.
remediation: For each ExternalName Service in the mesh: make sure the name it points to exists as a Service or ServiceEntry (a VirtualService routing to the ExternalName otherwise breaks), move any DestinationRule from the ExternalName host to the referenced host, and drop `ports` on the Service (now ignored). To opt out for one release set `ENABLE_EXTERNAL_NAME_ALIAS=false` on istiod (removed in 1.24).
verifyCommand: kubectl get svc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.type == "ExternalName") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " -> " + .spec.externalName'  # each printed Service is now an alias: its VirtualService/DestinationRule must target the referenced host

title: The `istio.io/gateway-name` label on Gateway-API gateway pods becomes `gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name`

detection.reason: checked on workload and Service selectors; a NetworkPolicy podSelector or a policy `selector.matchLabels` that keys on the label is named by the verify command

quote: the label key used to identify the gateway name is changing from `istio.io/gateway-name` to `gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name`. The old label will continue to be appended to the relevant label sets for backwards compatibility, but it will be removed in a future release.
remediation: Both labels are present from 1.21, so nothing breaks yet; istiod keeps the old key in the selectors of the Deployments and Services it manages. Change every selector, NetworkPolicy, AuthorizationPolicy and script of your own that keys on `istio.io/gateway-name` to `gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name` before 1.24, which removes the old label.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,svc,netpol,authorizationpolicies.security.istio.io,peerauthentications.security.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(tojson | test("istio.io/gateway-name")) | .kind + " " + .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # every printed object selects on the old label and must move to gateway.networking.k8s.io/gateway-name before 1.24

title: EnvoyFilter `applyTo: BOOTSTRAP` patches are no longer applied (they only ever were on proxies opted in with `BOOTSTRAP_XDS_AGENT`)

detection.reason: checked on the applyTo of every EnvoyFilter config patch the agent collects

quote: **Removed** using BOOTSTRAP_XDS_AGENT experimental feature to apply BOOTSTRAP EnvoyFilter patches at the startup.
remediation: Bootstrap patches were opt-in: only proxies started with `BOOTSTRAP_XDS_AGENT=true` (proxyMetadata) ever applied them, and those lose them at 1.21 when the flag is removed. For each listed EnvoyFilter, move the bootstrap customisation to a custom bootstrap ConfigMap (`sidecar.istio.io/bootstrapOverride`) or `proxy.istio.io/config` and drop the patch; a mesh that never set the flag has nothing to lose.
verifyCommand: kubectl get envoyfilters.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.configPatches[]?.applyTo] | index("BOOTSTRAP")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed EnvoyFilter carries a BOOTSTRAP patch that 1.21 proxies ignore

title: `istioctl install` no longer writes the `installed-state` IstioOperator, nor installs its CRD

detection.reason: what a script reads after install is not on the cluster; the CRD's presence only says a previous install created it

quote: As there is no `IstioOperator` needed for these usages anymore, `istioctl install` and `helm install` no longer install the `IstioOperator` CRD. Note this only impacts `istioctl install`, not the in-cluster operator.
remediation: Tooling that reads the `installed-state` IstioOperator (or expects the `istiooperators.install.istio.io` CRD after a plain `istioctl install`) must instead read `istioctl manifest generate` output or the live objects. In-cluster operator installs are unaffected.
verifyCommand: kubectl get istiooperators.install.istio.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | startswith("installed-state")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed installed-state object is a leftover snapshot that 1.21 stops maintaining

title: `PILOT_ENABLE_INBOUND_PASSTHROUGH` is removed — inbound passthrough can no longer be turned off

detection.reason: checked on the istiod Deployment's container env NAMES only — a flag set through `pilot.env` in a values file lands there; one set via `meshConfig` or an IstioOperator that has not been applied yet is not scanned

quote: **Removed** the `PILOT_ENABLE_INBOUND_PASSTHROUGH` setting, which has been enabled-by-default for the past 8 releases.
remediation: Remove the variable from istiod. If it was set to `false`, sidecars go back to inbound passthrough at 1.21: inbound listeners no longer rewrite to `127.0.0.1`, so applications that only bound to localhost need `Sidecar.ingress[].defaultEndpoint: 127.0.0.1:<port>` instead.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release)/pilot"))) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("^(PILOT_ENABLE_INBOUND_PASSTHROUGH)$")) | $n + ": " + .name + "=" + (.value // "(valueFrom)")'  # a printed line is the removed flag; a value of false means inbound listeners change to passthrough at 1.21

title: The legacy EnvoyFilter telemetry implementation and its `configOverride` values are gone

detection.reason: the removed fields are Helm values; only the EnvoyFilters an old install rendered from them are visible on the cluster

quote: the following fields are no longer respected: `prometheus.configOverride`, `stackdriver.configOverride`, `stackdriver.disableOutbound`, `stackdriver.outboundAccessLogging`.
remediation: Installs that still set `telemetry.v2.prometheus.configOverride` or the `stackdriver.*` values (rendered as the `stats-filter-*` / `tcp-stats-filter-*` EnvoyFilters in the root namespace) lose those customisations; express them through the Telemetry API (`metrics.overrides`) and remove the values.
verifyCommand: kubectl get envoyfilters.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^(tcp-)?stats-filter-")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed EnvoyFilter is the legacy telemetry implementation; its configOverride customisations are not honoured at 1.21

title: JWT authentication moves to Envoy's upstream filter — custom filters reading the `istio_authn` metadata key stop seeing claims

detection.reason: the agent ships an EnvoyFilter's patch enums and filter NAMES, never the patch value where `istio_authn` would appear

quote: Note that a custom Envoy or Wasm filter that used `istio_authn` dynamic metadata key needs to be updated to use `envoy.filters.http.jwt_authn` dynamic metadata key.
remediation: An EnvoyFilter (Lua, ext_authz, RBAC shadow rules) or WasmPlugin that reads JWT claims from dynamic metadata under `istio_authn` reads nothing once the proxy runs 1.21 — authorization decisions built on those claims fail closed or open depending on the filter. Change the metadata namespace to `envoy.filters.http.jwt_authn`. The switch is gated on proxy version, so a mixed fleet needs both keys until every sidecar is on 1.21.
verifyCommand: kubectl get envoyfilters,wasmplugins -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(tostring | test("istio_authn")) | .kind + " " + .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed filter reads the old metadata key and sees no claims from 1.21
